chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Armstrong splits from Collins and teams up with Joe Glaser
summary: Armstrong learns the cost of power of attorney, tells Budd he will go with Glaser who is leaving prison, and Glaser builds an empire.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: See? But anyway, we came on back to Chicago. Well, Louie, then, went to Europe, and him and Collins, and they got into some kind of thing, like coming back on the boat, and Collins called him a nigger, and all of that, and Louie got mad, and so Louie split from Collins, somehow or another.

But you see Collins -- then this is when Louie learned about the power of attorney, because when he split and left Collins, Collins took his car, and took everything that he had connected with Louie, that he'd accumulated. And so we used to go by and see Louie after this, you know, and he would be sitting up, he'd say, "That's all right." He says,

"Rockwell want me to re-sign with him. He offered me $5,000.00 to sign a contract." He said, "But I'm not going to sign with him." He says, "You know what I'm going to do? Old Joe Glaser's getting out of the penitentiary." He say and he ain't got nothing." And he says, "And I can tell him what to do, because he ain't got nothing."
Because he had been in jail, right?
Joe had been in jail. You know what Joe went to jail for?
Joe used to try to pimp off a black girls in Chicago, and he killed a guy over this black prostitute, and was sent to the penintentiary.

So when he came out, Louie says, "I'm going to get Joe Glaser, because he ain't got nothing. We both can start out together." And see, of course Joe Glaser's people owned, I think, the ground that the Sunset was setting on, that building. So therefore he was -- they are entitled him -- they let him collect the rent for that property, which paid him something like -- hm -- $150.00 a month, something like that. I don't remember the exact figure, and with that money, and with his being slick, being from the street, and everything, and being a hustler, took Louie Armstrong and built an empire.
I just want to hold you here for a second, because we've got right up to this empire, which is great, and most of us know the story, and let you get back to that.
But I wanted to ask you something about --
